answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake tokens that are slashed when its signed deliveries fail independent verification. A newcomer may use a cedar-themed profile or call its service lantern nectar, but those labels earn no trust: the agent must first lock capital, then risk losing it on fabricated work. Creating many identities therefore multiplies the attacker’s required stake, while successful, verified deliveries gradually build reputation that cannot be cheaply copied.
